A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
heat stress affects uteroplacetal circulation by increasing endothelin-1, which activates the prostaglandin system, resulting in the vasocontriction of the uteroplacentral circulation.
heat stress induces placental endothelin and prostaglandins, which are involved in the pathogenesis of uteroplacenta circulatory disturbances and subsequent placental dysfunction.
heat stress affects endothelin receptor and PGE2/PGF2alpha systems in the placenta, which may lead to the disturbance of uteroplacetal circulation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the activation of endothelin-1 receptors is a key factor in the vasocontrictive effects of endothelin during heat exposure.
heat stress may cause placental circulatory disturbances by increasing the production of PGF2alpha via activation of endothelin receptor.
heat stress can affect uteroplacetal circulation and the placental production of PGE2 and its metabolites, PGEM, and PGF2a and its metabolites PGFM.
